papers.summary: We develop a flow-map framework for nonlinear transport equations, comprising a self-consistent exact frozen flow and its numerical realization. An exponential--pullback identity represents each frozen transport exponential in a commutator-free exponential integrator as the pullback induced by its exact backward characteristic map. Composing these maps defines the self-consistent exact frozen flow, a time-discrete construction with autonomous frozen fields formed from linear combinations of transport fields evaluated at the stage approximations. A local freezing-error identity and a one-step estimate for the Lie--Euler Vlasov--Poisson update separate field variation, field approximation, and characteristic integration errors; these estimates do not assert global PDE convergence. We specialize this construction to the Vlasov--Poisson system and obtain the self-consistent numerical flow through velocity-space quadrature, a discrete Poisson solve, field interpolation, and numerical integration of the frozen characteristic equations. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we prove that the self-consistent exact frozen flow for this system is a volume-preserving diffeomorphism. Temporal self-convergence tests on Vlasov--Poisson and guiding-center benchmarks yield rates consistent with the design orders and illustrate conservation behavior and the evolution of solution structures in long-time simulations with large time steps.

papers.title: Byzantine-Robust Sparse Regression with Missing Covariates
papers.summary: We study distributed sparse linear regression with missing covariates and Byzantine workers. Correcting for missing observations can make the regression loss nonconvex, while Byzantine reports can distort gradient updates and impair estimation. A communication-efficient method is proposed that combines robust gradient aggregation with folded-concave regularization. Under appropriate regularity conditions, after $t$ communication rounds the estimation error is bounded by a transient component determined by the initial error and decaying geometrically with $t$, plus a residual component reflecting finite-sample variability and Byzantine contamination. Simulations and two real-data examples evaluate estimation accuracy, variable selection, and communication costs.

papers.title: The Intermediate Silicon Tracker Detector for sPHENIX
papers.summary: A new barrel-type silicon detector has been constructed in the central rapidity region of the sPHENIX experiment as part of its charged-particle tracking system. The detector, referred to as the intermediate silicon tracker (INTT), provides single-event timing capability and contributes to charged-particle tracking in combination with the silicon-pixel vertex detector and the time-projection chamber. The INTT consists of two cylindrical barrels with full azimuthal coverage. The inner and outer barrels comprise 24 and 32 silicon strip ladders, respectively. Each ladder consists of four silicon strip sensors, covering the pseudorapidity range $|η| < 1.07$ for collision vertices within $\pm~10$ cm along the beam axis, at radial distances between 72 and 103 mm. The INTT has been fully integrated into the sPHENIX data acquisition system, with detector signals processed by eight FELIX servers. Continuous data taking is enabled by a streaming readout mode, in which detector data are accumulated without hardware triggers, while a conventional trigger-based mode is also supported. The detector achieves stable operation, small inactive area, and high efficiency, providing precise timing, tracking, and vertexing performance during the collection of beam-beam collision data.

papers.title: A Barnett-Like Effect in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.summary: The Barnett effect refers to the spontaneous magnetization or polarization of rotating matter via spin-orbit coupling, a fundamental phenomenon observed across a multitude of physical systems down to atomic scales. Here, we demonstrate that this effect extends to subatomic regimes within relativistic heavy-ion collisions, where the most vortical fluid ever created in terrestrial laboratories is produced and the orbital angular momentum is transferred to emitted hadrons via spin-vorticity coupling. By performing transport simulations spanning a broad energy range, we discover a nearly-linear scaling relation between the global spin polarization of $Λ$ hyperons and the source tilt angle extracted via two-pion femtoscopic correlations. This scaling reveals that global $Λ$ polarization induced by the local vorticity field is modulated by the inclined geometry of the produced strongly-interacting nuclear matter in these collisions. Supported by existing experimental measurements, our results unravel a geometry-modulated Barnett-like effect at the femtometre ($10^{-15}$ m) scale.

papers.title: Trim: Fee Level Matters More Than Skew in Lightning Routing
papers.summary: Lightning routing nodes lend their channel balance for a posted fee. Operators' tools move that fee with the balance around a hand-set level, and which part of the fee drives revenue is unclear. We present Trim, which models a channel as a two-sided inventory with costly refills. Its optimal fee is a level, set by demand and replenishment, plus a balance skew, the shadow price of liquidity. The level is first order: no fee rule beats the ceiling demand and replenishment set, and on exactly solved channels the best flat fee comes within $1.6\%$ of the optimum at the median, whereas a level off by a factor of two loses tens of percent. The skew is second-order insurance: it adds at most what the flow-balancing flat fee loses to refused forwards. So the level should be chosen: Trim's rule traces the revenue--success frontier, posts one level on every channel, and adds a skew only where refills stay frequent and costly. On a 2026 snapshot with synthetic payments, no tuned tool beats that frontier by over a few percent, and a skew changes gross revenue by a few percent.

papers.title: Reward-Guided RRT* for Budgeted Task and Motion Planning
papers.summary: Robotic missions involving spatially distributed tasks often require jointly selecting rewarding locations and planning feasible motions under limited travel budgets. This paper proposes Reward-Guided RRT*, a new sampling-based framework that constructs a budget-feasible mission through a sequence of locally joint task-selection-and-motion-planning stages, evaluated directly in the continuous state space, without requiring a precomputed task-transition graph. The method incrementally builds a mission using reward-guided RRT* searches, while a return-feasibility procedure ensures that each selected task can be visited without violating the mission budget. Experiments with increasing obstacle complexity and number of tasks show solutions comparable to VNS-PRM* while requiring substantially fewer sampled states. We also extend the framework to Dubins steering and evaluate it in CoppeliaSim with a scaled car-like robotic platform, demonstrating its ability to incorporate vehicle kinematic constraints.

papers.title: Probing the Collins effect at photon-photon colliders
papers.summary: We propose to study the Collins effect in the production of almost back-to-back unpolarized hadrons (mainly charged pions) by looking at their azimuthal distributions around the jet thrust-axis in the process $γγ\to h_1h_2X$. The quasi-real photons in the initial state can be emitted either by two scattering leptons or two charged heavy nuclei in ultra-peripheral collisions. We provide numerical estimates for kinematic configurations in principle accessible at the Future Circular Collider and at the planned experiments on ultra-peripheral collisions at the LHC. We find that the corresponding asymmetries can be sizable, even up to around 10-15%. The proposed measurements would thus shed light on the fragmentation mechanism of quarks into hadrons and, in principle, would allow one to distinguish among different existing models for the Collins functions.

papers.title: On memory effects in odd spacetime dimensions
papers.summary: We establish the existence of a new electromagnetic memory effect in all odd spacetime dimensions. This effect is a universal property of electromagnetic fields sourced by charged particles of constant momenta, appears at the Coulombic order and is directly related to the Weinberg soft theorem. We provide a unified derivation of this effect in all higher dimensions by evaluating the Maxwell constraint on a null plane at large, finite distance. We observe that in odd spacetime dimensions, the lightray integral computing the memory effect does not commute with the large-$r$ expansion. Our results necessarily assume that the lightray integral is taken prior to the $r \rightarrow \infty$ limit. The effect vanishes in the opposite order of limits, in agreement with previous results. We compute the Coulombic order electromagnetic memory effect for both massless and massive sources in all higher dimensions, explain its relation to the Fourier transform of the leading soft photon theorem and present a protocol for its measurement in a finite time parametrically larger than the distance of a detector from the sources. We conclude with comments on the generalization to gravity.

papers.title: Accelerated Push-Pull with Local Updates for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization
papers.summary: We consider decentralized stochastic nonconvex optimization over directed networks. Push--Pull provides an efficient decentralized optimization framework for such networks, but in the stochastic setting, gradient variance can slow its convergence and complicate the analysis of linear speedup. Motivated by this observation, we incorporate recursive momentum into stochastic Push--Pull for variance reduction, yielding the accelerated stochastic Push--Pull (ASPP) algorithm. Under mean-squared smoothness, we prove that ASPP improves the convergence rate of stochastic Push--Pull and achieves asymptotic linear speedup with respect to the number of agents. To further reduce communication, we develop LASPP, a local-update variant of ASPP that allows each agent to perform multiple local updates between communication rounds. We show that LASPP achieves an additional asymptotic linear speedup with respect to the number of local steps. With a suitable number of local steps, LASPP reduces communication complexity while maintaining the same stochastic gradient complexity as ASPP. Numerical experiments on real datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: From Specific Heat Bounds to Penrose-like Inequalities: A Unified Thermodynamic Perspective
papers.summary: Under explicit and physically motivated assumptions, we identify a local-to-global thermodynamic mechanism that organizes several previously disconnected inequalities on black holes. We first focus on asymptotically flat, static, and spherically-symmetric black holes, and provide a unified thermodynamic perspective on various Penrose-like inequalities. We also discuss the generalizations in asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes/branes. In holographic settings, these bounds imply monotonic behavior of normalized thermodynamic quantities in the dual field theory. Notably, one central integrated inequality can be established directly under the NEC in general static planar symmetric asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black branes. Our purpose is not to claim a fully general proof of the proposed local bounds, but to expose a unified structural perspective connecting local thermodynamic constraints to global geometric inequalities. Establishing the local bounds beyond the classes considered here remains an open problem.

papers.title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
papers.summary: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.

papers.title: An asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity
papers.summary: In this work, we construct an asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity. Starting from a linear choice of the reduced function, which yields an asymptotically conical Schwarzschild-like solution, we introduce a nonlinear deformation that preserves the leading asymptotic cone while producing an exact black hole solution with a de Sitter core and finite curvature invariants. We further establish the corresponding black hole thermodynamics for both solutions within the Hamiltonian and Wald frameworks. The entropy contains rational and logarithmic terms in the regular model, and both solutions satisfy the first law of black hole thermodynamics.

papers.title: NOMAD-EEG: Native Omni-Montage Adaptive Diffusion
papers.summary: Purpose. Electroencephalography (EEG) montages, channel counts and recording lengths vary widely, but most EEG foundation models are bound to the channel set and input length they were trained on. We aimed to build a generative EEG foundation model independent of the number, identity and order of electrodes and of the input length. Methods. NOMAD-EEG is a 12.0 M-parameter diffusion model that alternates state-space layers along time, without patches, with attention across electrodes identified only by their 3D scalp position. It was pre-trained on 147 h of unlabelled EEG from a single corpus and evaluated with frozen linear probes on ten datasets with 1 to 64 electrodes against seven foundation models run under one protocol, and on two unseen populations. Results. Despite its small size (12.0 M parameters against 69 M for REVE) and single pre- training corpus, NOMAD-EEG outperformed all seven foundation models on EEGMMIDB mo- tor imagery (balanced accuracy 0.442), Siena seizure detection (macro F1 0.622) and Bonn seizure detection (AUROC 0.999), had the highest accuracy of the seven compared models on TUEP epilepsy diagnosis (0.640) and, after fine-tuning, the highest \k{appa} (0.635) and weighted F1 (0.814) on TUEV event classification. It was the best of five models on P300 detection in autism with an unseen eight-electrode montage (AUROC 0.718). With only 5 of 19 electrodes, its mean AUROC fell only from 0.942 to 0.891. Conclusion. Identifying electrodes by position and modelling time without patches let one small model, pre-trained on one corpus, outperform much larger EEG foundation models on seizure detection, epileptiform event classification, epilepsy diagnosis and motor imagery.

papers.title: False-Alarm Improvements and Detection Trade-Offs in QML Intrusion Detection: A Secondary Analysis of the Kaissar Corpus
papers.summary: Published results in quantum machine learning for intrusion detection (QML-IDS) require joint interpretation of false-positive rate (FPR), attack true-positive rate (TPR), and evaluation provenance. We reconstruct operating points in the 25-entry frame selected by Kaissar and colleagues: 21 included articles, 20 identified documentary families, substantive methodological material consulted for 15, and 24 descriptive points from five. In one test-labelled comparison, a quantum support vector machine reduces FPR from 6.875% for random forest to 3.329%, while TPR decreases from 93.955% to 93.682%; both rates improve against three other comparators. In another study, a complete benign row identifies FPR as 12/6000 (0.200%), despite incomplete attack-side allocation that requires additional assumptions for TPR. Normalized matrices identify detection ranges rather than a unique aggregate rate. A uniform provenance rule separates training-described and test-adjusted results from six conditional illustrations whose independence remains unverified. The contribution is a reproducible interpretation of favorable comparisons and detection trade-offs, without converting descriptive results or hypothetical calculations into operational guarantees.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 2 figures. Supplementary material (15 pages) is available as an ancillary file. Reproducibility artifact: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23642804

papers.title: A PDE-Based Model of Runner Flow in Mass Participation Events
papers.summary: This paper presents a macroscopic approach for modeling pedestrian movement. A convection-diffusion partial differential equation (PDE) is described and used to model the flow of runners along a marathon course. A marathon is a good modeling case study for human movement because the location of runners is only known in sparse locations, so an accurate model is needed to know where people are at all times. As well, marathons offer many safety and logistical problems that can be solved by modeling human movement. Data is obtained from the 2023 Columbus Marathon, and model improvements are made to include a temporally varying convection term. Results show an increase in model accuracy which can allow for better resource allocation and safety measures.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the 2026 Modeling, Estimation and Control Conference (MECC)

papers.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
papers.summary: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 9 figures. Dataset and accompanying resources available on Hugging Face under the HelmholtzAI-FZJ organization

papers.title: Comparing Measurements of Pictorial Depth: Conditions for Placing Methods, Observers and Depiction Styles on One Scale
papers.summary: Two observers can agree about what lies in front in a picture yet report different amounts of apparent depth. People report pictorial depth by judging which of two points looks nearer, setting a probe to match a surface, adjusting relative sizes, or rating three-dimensionality. Two such methods can agree closely without sharing a unit. We ask when different methods, observers, depiction styles and viewing conditions can share one scale. Each set of scores, a measurement block, is a graph node. Two blocks are linked only if their shared observations pass six checks fixed in advance, among them outcome type, removal of declared offsets and position effects, proportionality and covariance. If the adjusted shared patterns are exactly proportional, a connected graph fixes every block's gain, its relative scale factor. The checks accept proportionality only within a set margin, so a link supports the gains without proving exact proportionality. One unit is still not one depth coordinate. Suppose each block scores shared stimuli with its own origin and positive unit. A matrix-rank test then decides when a common coordinate is identified: when only one overall origin and unit remain free. If each shared stimulus, an anchor, is scored by exactly two blocks, this needs two disjoint sets of anchors, each connecting every block, their compatibility assumed, not tested. They also suffice, except for anchor values satisfying exact polynomial relations (probability zero for anchor values drawn from any distribution with a density). We adapt network gain estimation from test linking, with a loop-consistency check. A reanalysis of published probe settings on 3-D renderings passes one of 171 candidate depiction-style links through all six checks, each judged by its own 95% bound, unadjusted for the 171 pairs. Links between tasks remain untested; they need shared stimuli and a joint uncertainty model.
papers.comment: 32 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Ancillary files: reproduction package (anc/run_all.sh) with the graph enumeration, exact rank checks, simulations and seeds, and fetch and analysis scripts for the reanalysed public dataset

papers.title: Can Open Be Too Open? On the Security and Trustworthiness of Fully Transparent LLMs
papers.summary: There are different levels of transparency for LLMs: open weights, open data, and/or open pipeline. Recently, more interest has emerged in fully transparent LLMs, i.e., LLMs with fully open weights, data, and training pipeline. Drawing analogies to other fields such as software security, it is often believed that increasing transparency inherently increases the security and trustworthiness of the LLM. However, we argue that such claims need to be critically re-evaluated in the context of LLMs. In this paper, we analyze the impact of transparency on LLM security and trustworthiness by reviewing the relevant literature. Our core findings are that, due to the limited reproducibility of LLM pipelines, in practice, users cannot verify the correspondence between open weights and the associated open data and pipeline. Thus, in order to trust a model, users still need to trust that developers acted honestly, reducing the benefits over models that provide less "transparency". Moreover, we find that even when LLMs are fully transparent and trusted, this openness can favor adversaries. Open weights in particular, but also open data and pipelines, can increase the success rate of attacks. Although the same mechanisms can be used to improve the model and protect it against attacks, the current lack of robust lightweight mechanisms to patch LLM vulnerabilities limits the benefits of openness at this time. We note that our analysis is based on current LLM capabilities and analysis tools, and that future developments may require a re-evaluation of these points.

papers.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
papers.summary: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may invalidate earlier verification results and make human oversight less effective. This survey presents an operational definition and process framework for RSI and organizes the requirements for trustworthy RSI into four interconnected themes: genuine and sustained improvement; behavioral constraints, alignment, and fairness; system security and privacy; and transparency and controllability. We examine these themes from three perspectives: Improvement Validity, Constraint Preservation, and Effective Oversight. This analysis covers improvement diagnosis, proposal generation, proposal evaluation, and update implementation (S1--S4), including the recursive application of these stages to improvement mechanisms (RI). We review risks, safeguards, and evaluation evidence for individual updates, effects inherited by successor systems, and revisions to improvement mechanisms, while distinguishing direct RSI findings from evidence in related systems. Finally, we examine evaluation settings, identify requirements for independent and longitudinal assessment, and discuss applications and open research problems.

papers.title: Right Model, Right Task: Capability-Constrained Carbon Labeling to Decarbonize Generative AI
papers.summary: The carbon footprint of generative-AI inference depends not only on hardware efficiency and electricity supply, but also on whether the selected model is appropriate for the task. A frontier model may expend unnecessary computation on a routine request, whereas an under-capable model may increase energy use through failure, retries, extended reasoning and escalation. However, a standardized evaluation framework that accounts for task-specific capability requirements and the carbon emissions associated with successful task remains lacking. In this Perspective, we argue for a capability-constrained carbon labeling framework that shifts environmental assessment from carbon intensity per inference towards the expected carbon emissions per successfully completed task at the required capability level. Under this framework, models would first be assessed against task-specific capability requirements, and only models capable of meeting those requirements would be compared on their expected energy use and operational carbon emissions. By linking service quality to carbon cost, this approach could enable more informed matching of the right model to the right task, offering a demand-side pathway to reducing emissions associated with generative-AI token use. Realizing this vision will require standardized capability-based service assessments, comprehensive energy accounting and transparent carbon disclosures.

papers.title: Fast Calibration of Generalized Posteriors via Dirichlet Reweighting
papers.summary: While generalized Bayesian inference offers a principled approach to uncertainty quantification under general loss functions, its practical performance depends critically on the choice of the learning rate. Generalized posterior calibration, which selects the learning rate so that the resulting credible sets attain nominal frequentist coverage, is computationally intensive because it relies on repeated posterior sampling across bootstrap datasets and candidate learning rates. To overcome this practical difficulty, we propose a fast calibration method that combines Dirichlet-weighted bootstrap perturbations with importance sampling to estimate coverage while reducing the need for repeated posterior sampling. We further extend the framework to hierarchical models, where group-specific learning rates are calibrated and stabilized via shrinkage. Illustrative examples using quantile regression, support vector machines, and hierarchical Huber regression demonstrate that the proposed method substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining accurate calibration.

papers.title: Complete characterization of internal-external entanglement trade-offs in two-mode Gaussian states
papers.summary: We characterize the exact trade-off between internal and external entanglement in asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states at fixed local symplectic eigenvalues. Internal entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the two modes, while external entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ across a Gaussian purification. Numerical sampling suggests the boundary structure of the attainable region in the $(\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD},\mathcal{N}_{A:B})$ plane, which we then determine analytically. Parametrizing the global symplectic spectrum yields a closed admissible interval for the remaining spectral parameter at fixed $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$. We prove constructively that every point in this interval corresponds to a physical covariance matrix, implying that all intermediate values of $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the resulting sharp bounds are achievable. The upper bound is attained for opposite-sign correlations of equal magnitude, while the positive branch of the lower bound occurs when one global symplectic eigenvalue equals unity. We also identify two external-entanglement thresholds, derive a saturated monogamy-type inequality, and recover the symmetric-state limit.

papers.title: Adaptive Control for General Nonlinear Stochastic Systems
papers.summary: This paper extends the least-squares and certainty-equivalence minimum-variance framework of classical linear self-tuning regulators to a broad class of nonlinearly parameterized systems with compact parameter spaces, including commonly used deep neural network models. First, historical nonlinear least-squares fitting guarantees are converted into online one-step prediction bounds under a general modulus of continuity, with explicit regret rates under parameter Lipschitz continuity and finite-moment noise. Second, approximate NLS estimation combined with certainty-equivalence control achieves closed-loop stability and asymptotically optimal tracking under mild conditions without requiring excitation or parameter identifiability. Explicit closed-loop regret and tracking error rates are established in the parameter-Lipschitz case, and closed-loop examples show that the regret rates cannot, in general, be improved for this regulator. Finally, robustness to small unmodeled dynamics is established by showing that closed-loop stability is preserved and the tracking error bounds comprise a vanishing term and a residual term determined by the model discrepancy.

papers.title: Shape-Preserving Treatment Effects for Functional Outcomes
papers.summary: By recording health measurements daily rather than at a few clinical visits, connected devices pave the way for more precise real-world evidence that measures how the effect of an intervention unfolds over time: does the response rebound, peak late, or oscillate? Yet causal methods for such functional outcomes remain scarce, and those that exist target the Functional Average Treatment Effect (FATE). Its pointwise averaging flattens the features patients share whenever their curves are misaligned in time, as is common with biosignals, where patients respond with their own timing. We develop a causal inference framework that captures the shape of the effect of a binary intervention, based on the phase-centered elastic mean from elastic shape analysis. We lift this mean from a sample statistic to a functional of the data-generating law and prove that it is well defined under explicit geometric assumptions. Because it is not linear, it yields three causal estimands instead of one: populational, individual and local. We identify the populational estimand by inverse-probability weighting and the local estimand through the conditional outcome laws, estimate them by weighting and by matching, and show that the individual one is not identifiable. On simulations with timing variability or heterogeneous effect shapes, our estimators recover the shape that the FATE loses. On real weight trajectories following GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation, they reveal a rebound that the FATE averages away. This framework thus gives clinicians a treatment-effect curve whose shape and timing reflect genuine patient trajectories rather than a misalignment artifact.

papers.title: Synchronization-Oriented Multi-Radius BMOCZ for Non-Coherent Short-Packet Communications
papers.summary: Modulation on conjugate-reciprocal zeros (MOCZ) is a promising candidate for blind short-packet communication (SPC) in future wireless systems; however, its performance is sensitive to timing and frequency synchronization errors. In this paper, we propose a novel scheme named multi-radius binary MOCZ (MR-BMOCZ). This method introduces a new root placement strategy that enhances diversity in the autocorrelation domain. The resulting structure enhances the autocorrelation properties of the transmitted waveform, leading to improved timing offset (TO) estimation. Moreover, the multi-radius construction distributes the signal energy over a larger set of radii, hence reducing the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). The resulting waveform also exhibits a distinctive spectral structure that is exploited for carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation and correction, yielding lower normalized mean square error (NMSE) compared with BMOCZ-based schemes. Simulation results over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and fading channels demonstrate that MR-BMOCZ achieves superior synchronization performance while maintaining comparable bit error rate (BER) and block error rate (BLER) performance. Consequently, the proposed scheme offers a synchronization oriented extension of BMOCZ for robust non-coherent SPC.

papers.title: Multiplex relational event models of self-reported and perceived gossip
papers.summary: Gossiping is a complex social phenomenon that unfolds through multiple types of relations. Among other things, individuals may initiate gossiping about others as a result of believing themselves to be the target of gossip. These two processes, i.e., gossiping and gossip perception, form a dynamic multiplex network, where self-reported and perceived gossip ties coexist and can influence each other over time. We develop a multiplex relational event model to study the joint evolution of these two processes. The proposed model includes endogeneous covariates that capture the influence of events occurring within one layer, as well as events occurring on the other layer, on the rate of self-reported and perceived gossiping. We analyze survey data collected annually from 44 secondary schools in Hungary. We show how a multiplex relational event model, including linear, smooth and random effects, is able to describe the social mechanisms operating within and between self-reported and perceived gossiping and to capture how these two layers influence each other over time.

papers.title: The mathematical journey of spatial reciprocity
papers.summary: Over the past three decades, evolutionary game theory in structured populations has witnessed explosive progress. Counterintuitive cooperative phenomena discovered in simulations have stimulated the development of rigorous mathematical theories to describe the underlying dynamics. In this paper, we review these theoretical advancements, including pair approximation and coalescent theory, which offer analytical solutions to evolutionary games on networks. We summarize the key results obtained by these theories, while also discussing their limitations, such as high computational complexity and constrained flexibility when applied to complex models. We therefore suggest that mathematical approaches provide a complementary tool for understanding cooperation in structured populations alongside simulations.

papers.title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and neutrino opacities in hot dense matter
papers.summary:
We calculated the diffusion mean free paths of electron neutrinos and antineutrinos in hot, neutrino-trapped matter containing $Δ(1232)$ isobars, as found in proto-neutron stars and neutron star merger remnants. We included charged-current absorption with the $NΔ$ weak vertex of weak pion production, neutral-current scattering on all baryons and three-body antineutrino absorption on electron--baryon pairs, with relativistic mean-field kinematics. The reaction $ arν_e+e^-+n	oΔ^-$ dominates the antineutrino opacity whenever the neutron and electron chemical potentials exceed the in-medium $Δ^-$ rest energy, even where the $Δ$ population is negligible. At two to four times saturation density, where the reaction is open, it shortens the antineutrino mean free path from 
ubarLamNucMin--
ubarLamNucMax~m to 
ubarLamDMin--
ubarLamDMax~cm. Because antineutrinos are scarce at high lepton fraction, this changes lepton-number diffusion only at low lepton fraction, by up to \DtwoRedHi\% at these densities and by a factor of \DtwoRedLow\ at 1.5 times saturation density. For electron neutrinos, absorption on the $Δ^-$ and, at low lepton fraction, the opening of nucleonic absorption shorten the mean free path by factors of up to 
uRatioYLthreeMax\ at lepton fraction 0.3 and up to about 
uRatioYLoneMax\ at lepton fraction 0.1. We also showed that, for a given axial coupling, the spin of the $Δ$ reduces its Gamow--Teller strength per particle from 3 to $5/3$.

papers.title: SoK: Timestamps Are Not a Time Model: Rethinking Temporal Reasoning in Host-Based Intrusion Detection
papers.summary: Host-based intrusion detectors order events, window audit streams and sequence attack stages by their timestamps. Every conclusion they draw therefore rests on assumptions about clocks, delivery, entity identity and the integrity of the evidence, and most of these assumptions go unstated. This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) makes them explicit. Drawing on temporal databases, stream processing and runtime verification, we distill five components of a time model, together with a checklist of evidence assumptions and four levels of guarantee, and walk through a running campaign with them. A documented search yields fifteen families of detection and investigation. For papers selected by screening role and period, plus named systems and landmarks, we check the stated assumptions in the full texts, and we assess eleven temporal knowledge representation and reasoning (KRR) formalisms and a learned baseline on nine attack patterns. Some early alert correlators stated clock and delivery assumptions, and forensics measures clock error. Current provenance-based detectors state no clock bound. Four audited papers describe input-ordering conditions or conventions, but none specifies conditions for conclusion validity across a stated class of delivery failures. In the selected provenance-based systems, campaign composition uses system-specific procedures or objectives, learned state, causal graph queries or language models, and beyond CEP-based query systems, we found no temporal rule language or stream reasoner from KRR applied to host audit data. In 28 of 38 audited provenance-era detector papers, capture or stored evidence is trusted or its manipulation is placed out of scope, and none says which conclusions survive deleted, delayed or forged records. Five open challenges follow from these gaps.
papers.comment: Extended version with full appendices (search method, KRR domain analysis, rating evidence, formalizations). 51 pages, 1 figure, 16 tables. Artifacts: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23530002

papers.title: Dilepton azimuthal anisotropy from coherent $J/ψ$ photoproduction in hadronic Pb-Pb collisions
papers.summary: Hadron-based event-plane estimators can be affected by nonflow and autocorrelation biases, especially at low multiplicity. Coherent $J/ψ$ photoproduction offers a complementary geometry reference through the correlation between quasireal-photon polarization and the reaction plane. We calculate the second-order dilepton coefficient $A_2$ relative to the reaction plane in hadronic Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV within an equivalent-photon and generalized vector-meson-dominance Glauber framework. Nuclear diffraction and two-source interference produce a pronounced transverse-momentum dependence, while the rapidity dependence is weak. We also compare two treatments of coherent scattering in the overlap region of the two colliding nuclei. Suppressing the contribution from this region reduces the yield and strengthens the integrated polarization--reaction-plane correlation, with the largest differences in central and semicentral collisions and smaller differences toward peripheral collisions. Joint measurements of the coherent yield and $A_2$ can constrain how hadronic interactions disrupt nuclear coherence and clarify the photoproduction mechanism. With sufficient tagged yields, azimuthal correlations involving decay leptons from photoproduced $J/ψ$ mesons could complement studies of collectivity, with potential future applications to small systems.

papers.title: Dynamic conditional density network of wind vectors
papers.summary: We propose the dynamic conditional density network (DCDN) to correct the bivariate normal predictive distribution commonly used to postprocess ensemble forecasts of wind vectors. The conditional distribution of the observed wind vector given the ensemble forecast may depart from the bivariate normal distribution. DCDN multiplies a bivariate normal reference density by a correction density. The correction density is a B-spline mixture on the probability integral transform scale of the reference density, and a neural network predicts its weights. DCDN equals its reference density when the correction density is uniform. We apply DCDN to ensemble forecasts of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and observations at 154 sites in the Tohoku region of Japan. DCDN significantly improved the logarithmic score, energy score, and variogram score over the bivariate normal distribution predicted by a neural network. The improvement in the logarithmic score was large near zero wind speed and at higher wind speeds. This is consistent with non-normal features of the conditional distribution that the bivariate normal distribution misses.

papers.title: Scenario Matching for Credit Dependence Stress Tests: Temporal correlation constraints and empirical risk bounds
papers.summary: We couple two sets of simulated market and credit paths by minimizing absolute temporal-correlation error relative to a prescribed target. Each market path receives exactly one credit path, preserving both empirical distributions of complete scenarios. A perfect-matching test identifies whether a uniform correlation-error tolerance is feasible and determines its smallest attainable value. Further assignments give exact empirical mean-loss and exceedance-probability bounds; quantile bounds follow by binary search over eligible loss thresholds. A synthetic bond-forward credit stress test illustrates the method. The experiments report matching precision, empirical score tails and exposure-grid error, and measure matching and mean-loss computation. The method is independent of the scenario generator and provides a reproducible way to examine dependence assumptions in existing risk engines. Tail measures concern default-probability-weighted credit scores. Accompanying reproducibility package (Python code, synthetic scenario libraries, permutations, and benchmarks) is attached in the ZIP archive.

papers.title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing
papers.summary: In canonical twisted-torus models of hydromagnetic equilibrium in neutron stars, the toroidal field is confined to regions where the poloidal field lines are closed. As spindown torques applied at the stellar surface need not be communicated efficiently to such magnetically-unlocked regions, toroidal zones or magnetic voids may rotate faster than the electromagnetically braked part of the star. Continuous gravitational radiation from the associated non-corotating quadrupole may therefore be emitted at higher frequencies than poloidal ones to a degree that depends on the diffusive microphysics controlling angular momentum transport. Dissipative processes can suppress long-lived lags, and we estimate the relevant timescales and their sensitivity to microphysics. Nevertheless, we show that a quadrupole component whose pattern speed differs from the observed spin is shifted, or smeared, over a finite frequency band. Single-template or narrowband upper limits therefore constrain only the quadrupole contribution lying inside the searched frequency window, not necessarily the full frequency-integrated quadrupole. Using simple models, we quantify this spectral redistribution over finite observation windows and discuss its implications for continuous-wave searches.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Parkinson's Disease Classification from Resting-State Functional Connectivity
papers.summary: Altered resting-state functional connectivity (FC) is a candidate marker for the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD). Publicly available PD datasets, however, are small and fragmented across sites, scanners and clinical criteria. Transfer learning mitigates data scarcity by reusing a model trained on larger cohorts, but represents their knowledge primarily through a single set of weights shared by all individuals. Motivated by precision neuroimaging, we propose a retrieval-augmented classification (RAC) framework that additionally places each target individual in the context of similar individuals from external cohorts. A graph convolutional autoencoder (GAE), trained on external PD and control cohorts, encodes these cohorts into a neuro-knowledge base. Each target individual is encoded using the pretrained GAE, and its nearest neighbors are retrieved from the external knowledge base. Their embeddings are combined with the target embedding using mean aggregation or attention for classification. A systematic comparison on the TaoWu cohort separated the contributions of encoder pretraining, retrieval, attention and partial fine-tuning. Pretraining improved mean classification accuracy from 60.5% to 66.0%. However, retrieval and attention did not consistently improve performance over the pretrained-only variants. Several retrieval-based configurations nevertheless showed modestly higher ROC-AUC than the randomly initialized baseline. Varying the number of retrieved neighbors and partially fine-tuning the encoder provided no consistent additional gains. Retrieval-neighborhood analysis further showed diagnostically mixed neighborhoods. These findings provide initial evidence that population-learned representations can be complemented by individual-specific retrieval in neuroimaging, although larger datasets are needed to determine when such contextual information improves classification.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of thick branes in $f(R,T)$ gravity
papers.summary: We study tensor perturbations and quasinormal modes (QNMs) of thick branes in $f(R,T)=R+αT$ gravity. Starting from the background thick brane solutions, we derive the Schrödinger-like equation for gravitational perturbations and construct the corresponding effective potential. The effective potential exhibits a double-barrier structure whose properties depend on the model parameters. We analyze transmission spectra and find good agreement between resonance peaks and the real parts of the quasinormal frequencies. The parameters $b$ and $α$ mainly control the width and height of the potential barriers, respectively. QNMs are extracted using both time-domain evolution and direct integration methods, showing consistent results for low-lying modes. Higher overtones become increasingly difficult to extract due to stronger damping and numerical contamination. Our results indicate that $f(R,T)$ corrections significantly affect both the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum, providing a possible imprint of modified gravity in braneworld perturbations.

papers.title: CoSA: The Conflict of Skills Attack in Real-World LLM Agent Ecosystems
papers.summary: Agent Skills allow LLM agents to combine reusable capabilities, but checking each Skill in isolation cannot rule out policy violations when they are composed. We term such failures Conflict of Skills (CoS): artifacts or assessment signals produced for one purpose may be reused downstream without preserving the restrictions or authorization needed for their new use. Using controlled executions of publicly available Skills and matched single-Skill controls, we identify four recurring mechanisms behind CoS. Building on these findings, we introduce the Conflict of Skills Attack (CoSA), which adds locally admitted Skills to an existing pool to supply missing business operations (capability supplementation) or reshape artifact exchange, decision reuse, and target/action bindings (relationship reshaping). CoSA leaves existing Skills and runtime permissions unchanged. To evaluate this threat under autonomous Skill selection, we introduce CoSA-Bench, built from real-world Skills and controlled services, with 288 tasks across recruiting, finance, IT, and business, covering data leakage, unauthorized state modification, and unsafe execution. Across five LLMs and three agent harnesses, additions capped at 5% of each original pool raise the policy-violation rate from 35.02% to 58.45%, an increase of 23.43 percentage points. Trace analysis links compliant-to-violating transitions to cross-Skill dependencies involving the additions. Finally, we develop a lightweight harness-level guard that checks information flow and authorization before consequential actions. On OpenClaw recruiting tasks across five models, the guard reduces violations from 65.28% to 6.67%, while policy-compliant task completion on matched benign controls changes from 66.67% to 65.00%.

papers.title: GuardRAG: A Post-Retrieval Defense against Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances the factual grounding of Large Language Models (LLMs) by incorporating external evidence, but also exposes them to corpus poisoning attacks. In particular, coordinated attacks can introduce multiple mutually reinforcing poisoned documents into retrieved contexts, making reliable evidence filtering challenging. To address this problem, we propose GuardRAG, a training-free and plug-and-play post-retrieval defense that exploits the semantic structure of retrieved evidence to identify suspicious document groups. Specifically, GuardRAG first expands the retrieval range and removes near-duplicate candidates, then partitions the retained documents using Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HAC) with a query-adaptive threshold. Finally, it scores and prunes suspicious clusters based on query relevance, cluster size, and semantic compactness. Experiments across three question-answering datasets, multiple poisoning attacks, and six LLMs demonstrate that GuardRAG substantially reduces attack success rates while maintaining answer utility under clean retrieval.

papers.title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
papers.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into Web search, online recommendation, and intelligent decision-making, the third-party plugin ecosystem centered on model customization continues to grow. Among these, Steering Vectors guide model behavior by intervening in internal representations. However, the open plugin ecosystem also introduces new supply-chain security risks: malicious plugins can disguise themselves as having legitimate functionality and covertly manipulate outputs without significantly affecting model performance. Although this risk poses a real threat, the security issues of Steering plugins in the LLM supply-chain ecosystem still lack systematic research. This paper audits eight mainstream open-source Steering plugin libraries and reveals three structural vulnerabilities: insufficient distribution integrity verification, excessive plugin privileges, and missing runtime monitoring, which offers an attack surface for attackers. To investigate this threat, we propose a malicious plugin, IDH. Specifically, IDH designs a norm-gated mutually exclusive routing mechanism and proposes an information-decay inflection point localization method to automatically select the injection layer, thereby simultaneously achieving benign and malicious functions. To counter such threats, we propose a runtime defense framework, by suppressing anomalous activation interventions and orthogonalizing inter-layer trajectory. We evaluate IDH across five mainstream LLMs, using safety-refusal steering as the legitimate functionality and commercial recommendation manipulation as the hijack objective. Experiments covering six brands across three commercial domains demonstrate that IDH achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 97.8% while preserving high refusal rates on harmful requests.

papers.title: Martingality in EFM Signature Volatility Models
papers.summary: We establish a martingality criterion for the Exponentially Fading Memory (EFM) signature volatility model, extending the recent result of Abi Jaber, Gassiat, and Sotnikov (2026). In the proposed framework, the volatility process is given by a linear functional of the EFM signature of a time-augmented Brownian motion, which yields a globally well-behaved, fully non-Markovian volatility model admitting a stationary distribution. The stationary EFM signature volatility model is also covered by allowing for a random initial value of the signature. Moreover, the volatility process can be adjusted to the initial forward variance curve. For this model, excluding trivial cases, we prove that the price process is a true martingale if and only if the truncation order is odd and a sign condition involving the correlation parameter holds.

papers.title: The $C^0$-inextendibility of Kerr spacetimes
papers.summary: We prove the $C^0$-inextendibility of the full Kerr realizations considered in this paper and all their connected covering spacetimes. The result holds for positive mass and nonzero rotation in the subextremal, extremal, and overextremal regimes. The obstruction at the singular ring is expressed by unbounded proper time in a fixed-endpoint causal homotopy class. It persists under every positive continuous conformal rescaling and under continuous widening of the Kerr causal cones, without any global causality assumption. We give sharp bounds in a fixed coordinate norm for stationary and axisymmetric perturbations and describe complete timelike geodesics that encounter arbitrarily large curvature near the ring.
papers.comment: 78 pages, no figure. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Conformal Novelty Detection via Data-enhanced Localization
papers.summary: Novelty detection is an important area of research in both statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we focus on the conditional novelty detection problem, where novelties arise from the relationship between different variables. We first adopt the conformal inference framework and propose a data-enhanced localized conformal p-value, constructed by recalibrating an enhanced conditional distribution estimator. This estimator efficiently captures conditional information by incorporating both calibration and test data into its kernel estimation. We show that our p-values are valid in finite samples and can improve detection efficiency. Based on this p-value, we then develop a novel conditional novelty detection algorithm, along with a data-driven bandwidth selection method that ensures finite-sample false discovery rate control while enhancing detection power. Both simulated and real data experiments demonstrate the advantages of our proposed approach.

papers.title: Breakdown-Resistant Hierarchical Bayesian Calibration for Multi-Center Clinical Trials
papers.summary: Multi-center clinical trials are threatened by systematic location shifts in biomarkers measured across devices, sites, or reagent batches. Hierarchical Bayesian models are the standard remedy, borrowing strength across centers by pooling center-specific estimates. However, we prove that the standard Gaussian hierarchical posterior has a breakdown point of zero \emph{at the level of the posterior distribution itself}: a single contaminated center drives the posterior mean of every clean center to infinity and collapses the coverage of every clean center's credible interval to zero. We introduce the Posterior-Median Hierarchical Calibration (PMHC) framework, a fully Bayesian hierarchical model that replaces the Gaussian prior on center-specific shifts with a Laplace prior. Under absolute loss, the posterior median is the natural Bayes estimator, and we prove that its breakdown point is $\lfloor (K+1)/2 \rfloor$ contaminated centers---whereas the Gaussian posterior mean has breakdown point zero for every $K$. PMHC retains a full posterior distribution, enabling meaningful credible intervals and posterior probabilities. Across $K \in \{5, 10, 20\}$ centers and $n \in \{50, 200, 1000\}$ observations per center, PMHC maintains $94$--$98\%$ coverage under contamination fraction $ε= 0.60$, while Gaussian pooling collapses to $0.0\%$ coverage and its point estimate diverges by a factor of $54$. On real NHANES data ($n = 60{,}651$ across nine cycles), contamination in three cycles collapsed the Gaussian coverage to \(0.0\%\) and shifted clean cycles by \(0.41\) mg/dL, whereas PMHC maintained \(94.0\%\) coverage with a shift of \(0.008\) mg/dL. To our knowledge, this is the first explicit breakdown analysis of the \emph{posterior distribution} in hierarchical Bayesian pooling, and the first Bayesian model that is simultaneously contamination-robust and efficient in the clean-data regime.

papers.title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
papers.summary: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.

papers.title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
papers.summary: Automatic red teaming increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs) to iteratively diagnose failed attacks and propose improved adversarial prompts or injections. Although prior work strengthens this loop through prompt engineering and search-harness design, the mechanisms underlying its two core roles, criticism and attack proposal, has not been explored. To further investigate the core roles and therefore improve red teaming effectiveness, we disentangle two design choices: whether criticism is generated by the target session itself (self-criticism) or by a separately instantiated critic (external criticism), and whether that criticism is translated into the next attack by the target session (self-proposal) or by a separate attacker (external proposal). Through our analysis, we find that self-criticism is more effective because it is grounded in the target's live execution context, including observations, constraints, and available reasoning; removing reasoning reduces downstream attack success by 6%-17%. In contrast, self-proposal is substantially less effective because awareness of the adversarial objective induces explicit refusal and non-refusal sandbagging. These findings motivate a role-separated red-teaming approach: the target session diagnoses why an attack failed, while a separately instantiated attacker generates the next proposal. On DTAP-BENCH, spanning Telecom, Workflow, CRM, and Code domains, under both direct misuse and indirect threat models, as well as multiple agent frameworks, this configuration achieves 63.2% overall attack success rate (ASR), much higher than baselines. Our results show that effective automatic red teaming depends not only on model capability and search strategy, but also on how execution context and adversarial responsibility are distributed across model sessions.

papers.title: Intellectual Property Protection of Hyperdimensional Computing Classifiers: Black-Box Ownership Verification via Model Watermarking
papers.summary: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) offers efficient learning and inference for resource-constrained systems, yet ownership verification of its models remains underexplored. We present the first systematic investigation of model watermarking in HDC by adapting backdoor-based embedding to three classifiers with different prototype-learning mechanisms. Across four benchmarks, with conventional neural networks as references, we examine whether watermarks can be learned without compromising task accuracy and whether they survive subsequent model modification and replication. The error-driven classifiers, AdaptHD and OnlineHD, support verification at a nominal trigger exposure of 1% with at most 0.58 percentage points of mean accuracy loss, whereas single-pass Vanilla HDC requires greater exposure and can incur substantial accuracy costs. The error-driven models retain verification under native continued training, but extraction produces surrogates that reproduce much of the task behavior without verifiable watermarks. Watermark overwriting readily embeds attacker watermarks into HDC prototypes and erodes the owner's watermark more strongly than in the neural network references, although the strongest erosion coincides with large accuracy losses. We further deploy watermarked AdaptHD on an FPGA and stress its execution through undervolting and overclocking. Verification survives substantial computation errors, whereas more severe stress either causes verification failure together with accuracy collapse or results in inference timeouts. These findings establish the feasibility of watermarking in HDC while identifying limitations in retention under extraction and sensitivity to overwriting.

papers.title: Det-MASO: Diversity-Regularized Multi-Agent Sequential Optimization for Factor Generation
papers.summary: Quantitative investment requires alpha factors that are both predictive and diverse. However, existing factor generation methods, including formulaic mining and neural end-to-end models, are mostly based on a single-agent design, which limits exploration of the factor space and reduces adaptability to changing markets. Multi-agent approaches can broaden exploration, but agents trained under a shared objective often collapse to similar outputs, while existing diversity techniques either scale poorly with asset-universe size or address redundancy only after training. We propose a multi-agent sequential optimization (Det-MASO) framework for generating diversified, context-adaptive alpha factors. It introduces a differentiable log-determinant penalty on the inter-agent correlation matrix directly into the joint objective, discouraging correlated agent behavior during training with computational cost that scales linearly with the number of assets. We further show that this penalty prevents homogeneous equilibria and preserves factor diversity throughout optimization, while a context-conditioned scheduler dynamically adjusts agent emphasis across market regimes and Shapley interaction index analysis is used to characterize the cooperation structure that emerges among them. Experiments show that Det-MASO outperforms baselines, improving the information coefficient by 1.1\%, the annualized return by 6.4\%, and the Sharpe ratio by 0.33.

papers.title: A Certified Robustness Framework for Backdoor Poisoning Attacks using $f$-Divergences
papers.summary: Machine learning systems trained on untrusted data are vulnerable to data and backdoor poisoning attacks, in which an adversary corrupts training and test samples to manipulate predictions at inference time. Randomized smoothing yields provable defenses against such attacks, but existing applications to train-time robustness are limited to specific threat models and smoothing mechanisms. We propose a general framework that allows expressing complex adversary constraints on the number of corrupted training examples, feature and label perturbation magnitudes, and test-time corruptions. Our framework randomizes inputs by combining data subsampling with feature, label and test-sample noising. We develop a composable certification procedure based on $f$-divergences that handles arbitrary combinations of threat models and noising strategies, and recovers several prior certification regimes exactly as special cases. We demonstrate our framework experimentally by certifying, for the first time, robustness under general $\ell_p$-constrained poisoning adversaries under bagging with additive Laplace, Gaussian, and Uniform noises.

papers.title: What Will Replace Pull Requests? Rethinking Software Collaboration for AI Agents
papers.summary: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents has put pull requests under pressure: agents open millions of pull requests per month, while some open-source projects have begun to restrict or disable external contributions. We investigate which alternatives to pull requests practitioners are proposing or adopting and what these changes mean for empirical software engineering research. We reviewed 50 gray-literature documents from 31 organizations or individuals published between October 2025 and October 2026, coding the problems each named, the mechanisms it proposed or adopted, which of five roles of pull requests (integration, review, rationale, accountability, and external contribution) each mechanism takes over, and the evidence offered. Most responses retained pull requests in some form, whether by adding tooling, attaching a new artifact, or restricting access, and restriction was the response most often reported as adopted. Several proposed alternatives moved review and rationale into agent conversations and session records, but only Zed reported using a replacement in practice. Only two documents outlined a replacement for external contribution, and neither reported adoption. Pull requests are changing in ways that pull-request datasets will not capture: reviews conducted in agent conversations leave no pull-request comments, and projects that disable pull requests disappear from samples of newly opened ones. We outline a research agenda on the effectiveness of the emerging alternatives, their consequences for open-source participation, and the adaptation of empirical methods.

papers.title: A new categorical correlation measure
papers.summary: Feature screening in high-dimensional classification is an important problem in statistical learning, particularly in genomics, imaging, and other scientific fields, especially when the number of predictors exceeds the sample size. Zhong et al. (2024) present a semi-distance covariance (SDCov) as a dependence measure between a categorical random variable and a multivariate continuous random vector, presenting it as a promising tool for group-wise feature screening. However, SDCov is defined using the Euclidean norm, and its performance may be affected when the data is derived from heavy-tailed distributions or when outlier observations are present, which is a common phenomenon in high-dimensional data. This study proposes a modification of SDCov by replacing the $L_2$ norm with an $L_1$ norm. This adjustment results in a dependency measure between a categorical variable and a multivariate continuous variable that maintains the independence-characterization property of the original definition. Additionally, it serves as a robust and interpretable measure, particularly in the presence of outliers in the data. We establish the fundamental theoretical properties of the proposed measure and introduce a U-statistics-based estimator along with JEL-based inference for the measure. Additionally, we have introduced a test for independence based on the proposed measure. An extensive Monte Carlo simulation is performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed measure in comparison to existing measures in the literature. The proposed measure is applied in feature screening, as illustrated with the ADNI Alzheimer's disease dataset and the Iris dataset. The data analysis shows the proposed measure's effectiveness in identifying variables that facilitate strong class separation of the respective response variables.

papers.title: Attack logics, not outputs: Concept-based Property Attacks for Shortcut Elimination in Neural Networks
papers.summary: Deep neural networks (NNs) for computer vision are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, such that minuscule malicious changes to inputs may induce unintuitive outputs. One key approach to verify and mitigate such robustness issues is to falsify expected output behavior, which enables local robustness guarantees and adversarial training. Due to the black-box nature of NNs, current attacks only falsify a class of the final output, such as flipping from $\text{\texttt{stop_sign}}$ to $\neg \text{\texttt{stop_sign}}$. In this work we argue that robustness analysis should focus more generally on logical inconsistencies in concept-level reasoning rather than solely on output misclassification. We formalize this perspective through concept-based properties, i.e., constraints over human-interpretable concepts such as $\text{\texttt{red}} \land \text{\texttt{octogonal}} \implies \text{\texttt{stop_sign}}$ and study the falsification of such properties as a principled form of adversarial attack. Furthermore, an implementation of concept-based properties on already trained NNs is proposed using techniques from concept-based explainable artificial intelligence (C-XAI). For that we formally prove that attacks on concept-based properties are expected to have a reduced search space compared to simple class falsification, whilst arguably be more aligned with intuitive robustness targets. The practical effectiveness of our approach for logically informed adversarial training is shown in an empirical study across multiple models and datasets, including both vision and a security-relevant code processing task. Our results demonstrate that concept-level falsification generalizes classical adversarial attacks: Retraining on our novel attacks maintains robustness gains as compared to classical adversarial retraining whilst better eliminating semantic biases.

papers.title: Covariance spectra of random linear systems near instability
papers.summary: We study how stationary variance is distributed among the principal components of a randomly coupled linear system near instability. The coupling matrix has entries $N^{-1/2}ξ_{ij}$, where the $ξ_{ij}$ are independent copies of a bounded, centered real random variable of variance one. As $N\to\infty$ and the excess damping $δ_N\to0$, we prove that the covariance spectrum, with eigenvalues rescaled by $δ_N^2$ and weighted by their shares of the total variance, converges in probability to an explicit beta-product law. The convergence holds throughout $δ_N\ge N^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$ for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. The law describes eigenvalues of order $δ_N^{-2}$ at ranks of order $Nδ_N^{3/2}$. Its limiting rank profile decays as $r^{-4/3}$ at large normalized rank and determines how many principal components retain a prescribed fraction of the stationary variance. The proof combines an exact computation of planar moments, uniform estimates for growing matrix words that accommodate nonsymmetric entry distributions, and resolvent bounds controlling the contribution of long times.

papers.title: Accuracy and efficiency of compact foundation models for surface-water mapping during floods
papers.summary: Pretrained Earth observation models may reduce the effort needed to map surface water, but their value depends on the alternative against which they are compared. We evaluated Prithvi-EO-2.0-Tiny using the 446 hand-labeled Sentinel-2 chips from 11 flood events in Sen1Floods11. A fine-tuned model, a frozen-encoder model, and an identical randomly initialized architecture were compared with a similarly sized U-Net, a larger Prithvi model, and spectral-index thresholds. Experiments varied the number of training chips, excluded events from model fitting, and measured computational cost and prediction reliability. With 252 training chips, U-Net achieved a water intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.856 on the official test set, compared with 0.833 for fine-tuned Prithvi-Tiny. Pretraining improved the tiny transformer over random initialization by a reported 0.046 IoU with 25 training chips and 0.023 with 252 chips, but did not reverse the U-Net ranking. Across 11 event-exclusion evaluations, mean IoU was 0.768 for fine-tuned Prithvi-Tiny and 0.777 for U-Net; the paired interval included zero. Fine-tuned Prithvi-Tiny processed a 512x512-pixel chip in 16.1 ms on a GPU and 258 ms on a laptop CPU, compared with 30.6 and 665 ms for U-Net. Errors were concentrated near water boundaries, and high predictive entropy identified many, but not all, erroneous pixels. These results support a specific role for compact pretrained models: lower measured computational demand with competitive accuracy, rather than consistent superiority. Event-dependent performance, shared hyperparameter selection, and the distinction between observed water and newly inundated land delimit the conclusions.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables. Code: https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/Prithvi_Tiny_Floodwater_GeoAI Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23653544

papers.title: Explaining the universal Hagedorn temperature in string models of hadrons with fixed endpoints or baryon junctions
papers.summary: We derive the mass formulas and more accurate asymptotic expressions for the densities of states for string models of hadrons with one fixed heavy endpoint or a baryon junction. We show that strings with one fixed endpoint have the same Hagedorn temperature as ordinary open strings at the same tension and number of polarizations, despite the different Regge slopes of heavy-light and light mesons. This provides a microscopic explanation for the universality of the Hagedorn temperature recently found phenomenologically. We also find that the baryon-junction and quark-diquark pictures share this Hagedorn temperature and yield the same asymptotic mass dependence of the density of states, differing only by an overall normalization. The observed baryon mass spectrum provides little discrimination between the two pictures, although the baryon-junction model has a larger discrepancy with the observed Regge slopes.

papers.title: ECHOES: An Adaptive LLM-Powered AR Glasses Docent for Evidence-Grounded Urban Heritage Interpretation
papers.summary: Urban heritage tours are often delivered through fixed scripts, leaving limited room for visitors' situated questions, language preferences, or requests for evidence. We present ECHOES, an adaptive LLM-powered AR glasses docent for evidence-grounded interpretation of historical buildings. Specifically, the agent adapts along three dimensions: it modifies response structure according to the type of visitor question (identification, architectural detail, evidence-seeking, or route inquiry); it accumulates session-level interest signals from repeated questions and expressed curiosity to shape later explanations; and it tracks language preference and retrieval context across turns to maintain conversational continuity. The core of ECHOES is an LLM agent initialized as a source-aware urban heritage docent that realizes this adaptation through dialogue and preference context maintained across the session. Around this agent, ECHOES integrates visual site grounding, a self-built historical knowledge base supporting retrieval-augmented generation, and concise multilingual AR output designed for glanceable use. Through a working prototype centered on Shanghai's East Nanjing Road and the Bund, we demonstrate how an adaptive LLM-powered AR docent can transform historical tours from scripted narration into situated, question-responsive, and source-aware conversations.

papers.title: Cross-vehicle injury spillovers of ADAS functions in two-vehicle rear-end and same-direction sideswipe crashes
papers.summary: Advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) functions are evaluated mainly by the crashes they prevent, and little is known about how they relate to the injuries sustained in the crashes that would still occur. Because two colliding vehicles share one impact, a function on one vehicle may also be associated with the other driver's injury. This study examines whether an ADAS function on either vehicle in such two-vehicle crashes is associated with either driver's injury. It focuses on rear-end (n = 2,273) and same-direction sideswipe crashes (n = 1,216) from Texas police reports across 2023 to 2025. Striking and struck roles were assigned within each crash, and the ADAS functions of each vehicle were identified from vehicle identification numbers. For each crash type, a bivariate probit model, with random parameters for rear-end crashes, jointly estimates whether each driver was injured. Significant cross-equation correlations (0.559 and 0.375) support the joint specification. Electronic stability control on the striking vehicle is associated with a lower struck-driver injury probability in both crash types, by 0.036 to 0.073 in rear-end and 0.102 in sideswipe crashes. Lane departure warning on the striking vehicle shows a similar association in sideswipe crashes (about 0.078). Traction control with anti-lock braking on the struck vehicle shows the largest association among the ADAS functions with its own driver's injury probability (0.097 and 0.103 lower). No struck-vehicle function is associated with the striking driver's injury, and forward-looking functions show no association with either driver's injury, consistent with their benefit lying mainly in crash prevention. The findings suggest that the protective benefits of stability and lane departure functions may reach beyond the equipped vehicle to the other driver, strengthening the case for their wider fleet adoption.

papers.title: Cordon Tolls and Urban Traffic Volumes: Evidence from NYC's 2025 Congestion Relief Zone
